independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Independent re-derivation from the toolkit data confirms the row's core architecture and most of its counted claims exactly. Hallelu-Yah frame: psalm_device_inventory.json places oshb:Ps.150.1 as the 11th (last) of 11 verse-initial occurrences and oshb:Ps.150.6 as the 13th (last) of 13 verse-final occurrences (counts 11/13/1 verified against the full lists) — Ps 150 closes both the book and the frame inventory itself, apt for the row's closing-psalm reading. Imperative-token recount from the pointed bytes of oshb:Ps.150.1-Ps.150.6 (word-level, hand-recounted per verse) matches the row exactly: v1=3, v2=2, v3=2, v4=2, v5=2, v6=1, total=12; the opening token of 150:1 and the closing token of 150:6 are the 2 frame-anchors, leaving 10 internal — exact match to the row's 2/10 split. Instrument/sound-term recount across web:Ps.150.3-web:Ps.150.5 also matches exactly at 8 (shofar, nevel, kinnor, tof, minnim, ugav, two cymbal terms), correctly excluding the activity term "dancing" (v4) from the instrument count — sound object-naming discipline. No baruch/amen tokens occur anywhere in the six verses (direct read of all six), supporting the row's contrast with the book's four baruch-and-amen doxology seams. Numbering: ps_lib.web_to_mt confirms Ps 150 is an identity psalm for all six verses (WEB v = MT v, v=1..6), so the row's dual-citing, while not strictly mandated for an identity psalm, is harmless and correct. Book strategy Ps.md section 6 explicitly names 'coda' with 150 as the Psalter's closing doxology-psalm 'if argued' as the disclosed rival unit_type; the row engages this rival directly (its rejected_alternative) and rejects it on the textual ground that 150 shares no baruch/amen formula with the other four doxology seams — a legitimate, textually-grounded rival disclosure. On the SPAN (Ps.150.1-Ps.150.6, tiling confirmed exact, 6/6 verses, no gaps or overlaps) and the whole_psalm UNIT_TYPE call, the row is well-supported and I do not contest it. However, one specific factual claim in the warrant is false on re-derivation from the pointed bytes — see the challenge below; it narrows but does not overturn the boundary call.

challenges.claim: The rationale's claim of "no jussive, infinitival, or nominal-clause" register shift across the span is false: oshb:Ps.150.6 opens with a tav-preformative (prefix/imperfect) verb carrying jussive force, not the imperative pattern used in every other clause of the psalm.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.150.6 (byte tier, verified via collate.py --json against source): כֹּ֣ל הַ֭נְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּ֥ל יָ֗הּ הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ — its third word, תְּהַלֵּ֥ל (spliced from verse_map_oshb.json; byte tier), is a tav-preformative prefix-conjugation (imperfect) verb, functioning as an indirect volitive ("let it praise") with an explicit nominal subject two words earlier in the same clause. This is a different conjugation from the bare imperative pattern opening oshb:Ps.150.1, הַ֥לְלוּ, and from the imperative-plus-3ms-suffix pattern opening oshb:Ps.150.2, הַֽלְל֥וּהוּ — both spliced from source, both no-preformative, and both representative of all 12 imperative tokens recounted across oshb:Ps.150.1-Ps.150.6 (including 150:6's own closing token). WEB's own rendering of the clause, “Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!” (web:Ps.150.6), signals the same jussive/indirect-volitive force for the opening clause in translation ("Let ... praise"), distinct from the direct “Praise ...” imperative renderings used at web:Ps.150.1 through web:Ps.150.5 and for 150:6's own second clause. check_universals.py independently flags both the rationale's "no jussive, infinitival, or nominal-clause" phrase ([0].rationale) and the duplicate claim at observed_substrate_signals[4] ("throughout") as unswept universal claims with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep — consistent with this being a real, uncounted overclaim rather than a tool false-positive. Scope: the jussive shift is confined to the opening clause of 150:6 itself and does not create a rival verse-level strophe seam, so it narrows but does not overturn the row's whole_psalm span/unit_type call.
